title: Token ingest shortcut lane and attention-hint kernel advisor
creator: Ava Chen
description: Reduce prefill-side overhead for short-to-medium prompts by implementing a dedicated token-ingest fast lane and an attention-aware kernel advisor. This ticket scopes a runtime-level optimization that short-circuits common token normalization cases, uses a tiny LRU session prefix cache, and surfaces a light-weight advisor that picks kernels and attention tiling strategy based on token-length histogram and attention window patterns at prefill time. Goal: reduce per-request CPU and tail prefill latency for conversational short prompts without increasing memory footprint or breaking existing rollout invariants.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype integrated into serving runtime and gated behind config flag 'ingest_shortcut_v1'
End-to-end microbench shows >=15% median prefill latency reduction and >=20% 95th-pct tail improvement on short prompts (<=64 tokens) vs baseline on c5-gpu-equivalent infra
No regression (<1%) in decode latency or token accuracy on a random sample of production prompt set (5k prompts)
Automated unit and integration tests for shortcut path, cache eviction, and advisor decision logic
Documentation page in Confluence describing flags, trade-offs, and rollout plan
Canary rollout steps and rollback plan included in PR description

comments: 2025-02-10 Ava Chen: Initial RFC attached. Core idea: short-circuit ASCII-only, small whitespace-trim cases, avoid full grapheme segmentation for common prefixes; keep semantics identical for edge cases. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/INGEST-SHORTCUT-RFC

2025-02-12 Marcus Rivera: Implemented baseline shortcut path prototype in branch feat/ingest-shortcut. Microbench locally shows 18% CPU reduction and ~22% median prefill latency improvement for 16-64 token prompts. Pushed WIP PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/2124

2025-02-14 Riya Patel: Advisor prototype uses two heuristics: token-length histogram and attention window (global vs local). Early results: for long attention windows, kernel choice favors tiled attention; for short windows, stream-optimized kernels win. Need to calibrate cost model for switch thresholds.

2025-02-16 QA (Nina Gomez): Found a correctness regression for inputs with zero-width joiners when shortcut path applied. Reproduced with fuzz case; suggested adding grapheme fallback trigger when non-ASCII punctuation encountered. Marked as blocker until fixed.

2025-02-18 Marcus Rivera: Fixed ZWJ regression by adding 2-character lookahead and falling back to full normalizer. Added unit tests. Updated PR with tests and perf numbers. New microbench: 24% median and 27% 95th-pct improvement on short prompt set; cost of fallback negligible in sample corpus.

2025-02-19 Priya Nair (PM): Reviewed rollout plan. Requested canary at 5% traffic with telemetry for per-route tokenization hit-rate, cache hit-rate, advisor decisions, and rollback triggers if token-accuracy drops >0.5%.
2025-02-20 Marcus Rivera: Preparing canary PR and adding observability hooks. Draft runbook: /docs/runbooks/ingest-shortcut-canary.md. Targeting canary start 2025-02-25.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: more aggressive shortcut rules yield higher perf but increase risk of subtle normalization mismatches; we prefer conservative rules plus an explicit safety fallback.
Memory: the LRU session cache is bounded at 64 entries per serving worker to avoid OOM pressure during high concurrency.
Kernel advisor: lightweight decision path (constant-time heuristics) to avoid adding scheduling CPU overhead. Longer-term plan is to feed advisor metrics to Optimize for automated tuning.
Rollout: start with non-critical model families and routes (internal dev and low-qps customers) before platform-wide flip.
Related work: ties to ENG-314159 (normalizer microcache) and ENG-20988 (decode coordinator). Ensure we maintain compatibility with existing prefix caching semantics.
